title: deepAMP designs broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides active against resistant bacteria
summary: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates. More than 90% inhibited Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria better than the reference peptide penetratin; three candidates showed reduced resistance emergence in serial-passage assays and activity in a mouse Pseudomonas wound-infection model.
ai_technology: deepAMP peptide language model (deepAMP-general, deepAMP-AOM, deepAMP-POM and deepAMP-predict)
organization: Hunan University; Cleveland Clinic; National Cancer Institute; Tel Aviv University

evidence.tested: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates.
evidence.unknown: This is a separate discovery study from the AMPSphere microbiome-mining paper already in the tracker: deepAMP optimizes peptide sequences, whereas AMPSphere mined microbiomes. Testing involved 29 candidates and one female mouse wound model; this is preclinical evidence, not clinical efficacy. The article itself calls for more animal-model validation.
evidence.ai_role: The generative and ranking models optimized candidate peptide sequences for antimicrobial potency and membrane-disrupting activity. Researchers synthesized and tested selected sequences in vitro and in a mouse wound infection experiment.
